# The unit has no commit-confirm and no rollback: every value is live as soon as its Enter is
# accepted, and the configuration is written to flash when a top-level menu is left with ESC (any
# session that leaves one saves everything). tacctl types nothing: you do each step yourself.
# Before you start: keep the serial console, or a second session logged in as an Administrator, open
# until the check at the end passes; type /SN and make sure no other administrator is on the unit (the
# pull saw 1 other session).
# The way back is tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout: the old values.
#
# Type this first, on lab-unit, and check the version:   /H
# The title must read "COMMAND MENU: Version 8.10": tacctl's tables are those of that command menu,
# and another version may number its pages differently: stop. /J shows the unit's Site ID: the pull
# read wti.site.example.net; another one means this is not the unit.
#
##### DO THESE STEPS ON: lab-unit #####
# At the unit's prompt type /N and Enter. For each step type the item numbers of its second column,
# one at a time with Enter after each, then what the arrow says. A pick: the number of the line
# that reads as shown. ESC goes back one level. A value is live as soon as its Enter is accepted.
#  1. /N  31  Multiple Logins  -> 2 (On)   was: 1 (Off)
#  2. ESC ESC  leave /N: wait for "Saving configuration to flash"
##### END OF STEPS #####
#
# Check now. The unit has no rollback: nothing undoes this by itself.
#   From the tacctl server:   tacctl device config pull lab-unit --diff     (aaa: ok)
#
# To undo it: tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout (the steps with the values the pull
# showed; tacctl keeps this plan's back-out until the next plan with changes).
# Do not: paste anything outside the banners; paste a block into another unit; leave /N with ESC
# before the last step of the list; keep this output in a file after the paste when it holds a
# secret.
# Locked out (the paste cut your session and no login works)? A superuser runs: tacctl breakglass hold lab-unit --reason "..."
# then log in on the unit's serial console as its local Administrator account,
# fix or back out, and the superuser runs: tacctl breakglass release lab-unit
